standard.title: Create content with conventions
standard.description: use the core features of common digital tools to create, locate and communicate content, following agreed conventions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use basic features of digital tools to create, locate and communicate content (AC9TDI2P04). They have used digital tools for simple content creation. They have not yet worked with agreed conventions, information hierarchies, or search strategies for finding suitable sources.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use core features of common digital tools to create, locate and communicate content, following agreed conventions including safe search steps, file organisation and appropriate use of autocomplete features.

nodes.label: Finding information online safely
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can follow agreed steps to find information online using a search engine
nodes.minimum_width: Use a search engine to find information for a purpose following at least two agreed steps (e.g. use safe search, check the source is suitable)
nodes.typical_width: Follow a class-agreed set of steps for safe online information search; evaluate whether a source is suitable before using it; create a presentation or document drawing on located information
wider: Investigate how search results differ when using different keywords — discuss how word choice affects what is found and why some searches return unsuitable results
Compare how First Nations Australian community resources are represented in search results — discuss issues of representation and how to locate reliable culturally appropriate sources

response_modes.reason: Agreed steps for safe online search need to become habitual, not just known. Fluency and consistent application of safe practices — not breadth — is what matters at this node.

success_criteria: Follows agreed steps without being prompted
Selects a source that is appropriate for the task
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have not internalised safe search steps will bypass them under time pressure in N3 content creation tasks — the habit must be consolidated before it is needed automatically in a production context.

nodes.label: Organising content with hierarchies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can group, name and organise files and folders using a logical hierarchy
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least two folders with appropriate names and place files in the correct folder using a provided logical structure
nodes.typical_width: Design and apply a logical folder and file hierarchy for a class project; name folders and files consistently; explain why a given structure makes sense for the type of content
wider: Design a file hierarchy for a virtual library or virtual supermarket with multiple categories and subcategories — explain the organisational logic and how someone unfamiliar with the structure could navigate it
Compare a flat file structure with a hierarchical one for the same set of files — discuss which is easier to navigate and why hierarchy helps with larger collections

response_modes.reason: Students often create file names and folder structures without reasoning about navigability. The reasoning scaffold — 'what category does this belong to? what would someone search for to find it?' — builds an organisational logic rather than arbitrary grouping.

success_criteria: Files are placed in folders that match their content category
Folder and file names clearly indicate what is inside

nodes.label: Using core tool features to create and communicate
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use core features of a digital tool (including autocomplete) to create and communicate content following agreed conventions
nodes.minimum_width: Use a digital tool to create content for a purpose, applying at least one agreed convention (e.g. appropriate file name, correct folder, use of autocomplete)
nodes.typical_width: Create and communicate content using core tool features across different formats (presentations, documents, messages); apply agreed conventions consistently; use autocomplete features in text authoring tools appropriately
wider: Create content in a tool that is unfamiliar — apply the conventions learned in familiar tools and discuss which transferred and which required adjustment
Create content for a specific audience beyond the classroom (e.g. a presentation for parents or a guide for a younger class) — discuss how conventions change depending on the audience and purpose

response_modes.reason: Core tool features (file saving, naming conventions, autocomplete, folder use) need to be built across multiple tools and formats before they become transferable. Students who only practise in one tool often cannot apply conventions in a new one — repertoire across formats is the target.

success_criteria: Applies at least two agreed conventions in produced content
Content communicates the intended information clearly
